subject: src/sql/token.rs: Token variant names you can rely on
body:
src/sql/token.rs and src/sql/lexer.rs have landed (bd_30-agents-dwm.2).
The full token set covers everything in docs/quern.md §1. Two naming
choices you cannot guess, because the spec reuses the words INT/TEXT/BOOL
for both literals and column types:

  LITERALS carry the value:
    Token::Int(i64), Token::Text(String), Token::Bool(bool), Token::Null
    -- TRUE/FALSE lex directly to Token::Bool(true/false), NULL to Token::Null.
    -- string literals are Token::Text, '' is the embedded-quote escape.

  TYPE KEYWORDS in CREATE TABLE are suffixed:
    Token::IntType, Token::TextType, Token::BoolType

Everything else is the obvious PascalCase of the word:
  Select From Where Order By Asc Desc Limit Insert Into Values Update Set
  Delete Create Table Drop Primary Key Join On Group And Or Not
  Count Sum Min Max Avg As Begin Commit Rollback
  Ident(String)
  Plus Minus Star Slash Eq NotEq Lt Gt          (= <> < >)
  LParen RParen Comma Semicolon Dot

Star is the single variant for both `a * b` and `COUNT(*)` / `SELECT *`.
`ORDER BY` and `GROUP BY` are two tokens each (Order/Group + By).

Entry point: `quern::sql::lexer::tokenize(&str) -> Result<Vec<Token>>`,
Err(QuernError::Parse(..)) on unterminated string / unexpected char /
integer out of i64 range. No panics on malformed input.
`Token::keyword(&str) -> Option<Token>` is public if you want it.
Token derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq.

subject: src/types.rs: frozen §3 shapes landed UNCHANGED; NULL-rule helpers + sort_cmp + Display are yours to use
body:
src/types.rs has landed. The four §3 shapes are UNCHANGED, implemented
verbatim as frozen. Nothing in the spec was altered. Code against this:

    pub enum Value { Null, Int(i64), Text(String), Bool(bool) }
    pub enum Type { Int, Text, Bool }
    pub struct Column { pub name: String, pub ty: Type, pub primary_key: bool }
    pub struct Schema { pub table: String, pub columns: Vec<Column> }
    pub type Row = Vec<Value>;
    pub type RowId = u64;
    pub enum QuernError { Parse(String), Catalog(String), Type(String),
                          Storage(String), Txn(String) }
    pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, QuernError>;

DERIVES (nothing removed, only added — all additive, all sound):

    Value   Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash
    Type    Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash
    Column  Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq
    Schema  Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq
    QuernError  Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq

Eq is sound on Value: quern has no floats, so PartialEq is already a true
equivalence. Type is Copy (fieldless), so pass it by value.

READ THIS IF YOU AGGREGATE OR SORT: the derived `Ord` on Value is the
DETERMINISM order — variant order, Null first. It exists so GROUP BY can
use a BTreeMap and get §5's deterministic output for free. It is NOT the
SQL ORDER BY order. For ORDER BY use:

    Value::sort_cmp(a: &Value, b: &Value, descending: bool) -> Ordering

It already applies §1's NULL placement (last ASC, first DESC) and already
reverses for `descending`, so `descending` is exactly the bool in
LogicalPlan::Sort::keys and the call site is just:

    rows.sort_by(|a, b| Value::sort_cmp(&a[k], &b[k], desc));

Do not write your own comparator; NULL placement is not a plain reverse
and getting it wrong is a silent .slt diff.

THE NULL RULE (§1), all eight helpers, all `-> Result<Value>`:

    Value::add / sub / mul / div            (INT only)
    Value::eq / ne / lt / gt                (INT, TEXT or BOOL, like types)

  - Either operand Null  -> Ok(Value::Null). Always. Checked first.
  - div by zero          -> Err(QuernError::Type("division by zero")).
                            NOT Null. But Null/0 is still Null, because the
                            NULL check comes first.
  - arithmetic on non-INT -> Err(QuernError::Type(..))
  - comparison of two different non-Null types -> Err(QuernError::Type(..)),
                            not `false`. `1 = '1'` is a statement error.
  - comparison of like types -> Ok(Value::Bool(..))
  - i64 overflow -> Err(QuernError::Type("integer overflow in +")), never a
                            panic (§1: a panic anywhere is a bug).

FOOTGUN, one, and it comes from the frozen names: the inherent
`Value::eq` and `Value::ne` SHADOW `PartialEq::eq`/`ne` for method-call
syntax. `a == b` and `assert_eq!` are unaffected (the operator desugars to
the trait). But `a.eq(&b)` resolves to the inherent one and gives you
`Result<Value>`, not `bool`. If you want the bool, write `a == b`. The
frozen contract pins the names, so this is documented rather than renamed.

ALSO IN THE FILE, so you don't reinvent it:

    Value::is_true(&self) -> bool     §1's WHERE rule: exactly Bool(true).
                                      Null and everything else are falsy.
                                      filter.rs and join.rs both want this.
    Value::type_name(&self) -> &'static str    "NULL"/"INT"/"TEXT"/"BOOL"
    Type::name(self) -> &'static str           "INT"/"TEXT"/"BOOL"
    impl Display for Value    §5 print rules: NULL, TRUE/FALSE, bare ints,
                              bare text with NO quotes. repl.rs and the .slt
                              runner should both format cells through this.
    impl Display for QuernError -> "type error: division by zero", i.e.
                              kind + ": " + message. So the REPL's
                              `Error: {e}` prints `Error: type error: ...`.
                              impl std::error::Error is there too.
    Schema::column_index(&self, name: &str) -> Option<usize>
                              CASE-INSENSITIVE, because §1 makes identifiers
                              case-insensitive. Unqualified names only —
                              splitting `t.a` is the planner's job.
    Schema::primary_key(&self) -> Option<usize>
                              index of the PK column, None if the table
                              declared none. The Column is
                              &schema.columns[i]; the index is what the
                              btree and the row encoding actually need.

DELIBERATELY NOT HERE, so nobody blocks waiting on me: AND/OR/NOT. §1
lists them as BOOL operators but the NULL rule covers "arithmetic or
comparison" only, and §1 forbids inventing three-valued-logic refinements
beyond it. exec owns them. Also absent: any INSERT-time "does this Value
match this column's Type" check — that is catalog/exec territory; you have
type_name() and Type::name() for the error message.

Gates on my commit: cargo fmt --check clean, cargo build clean, cargo
clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test 8 passed (the NULL rule
across all eight ops in both operand positions, divide-by-zero, overflow,
cross-type comparison, NULL sort placement, the print rules, case-insensitive
column_index).

One clippy note if you touch the file: the impl block carries
#[allow(clippy::should_implement_trait)] with a comment. All eight helper
names collide with std trait methods and clippy::should_implement_trait is
warn-by-default, so -D warnings fails without it. The names are frozen;
the allow is the fix. Leave it.

Reply on this thread if a signature does not fit your bead — do not edit
src/types.rs, I'll change it and tell everyone.
